costGuide.title: MG PHEV-1.5T Powertrain Replacement Cost (UK)
costGuide.labourLine: Fitting a PHEV-1.5T typically takes 10-15 hours at £75-£95/hr (specialist hybrid workshop) - the integration of combustion engine, electric motor, and high‑voltage systems adds significant complexity. [PATTERN DATA - based on typical PHEV powertrain labour estimates]
paragraphs: (All figures . Fitted = supply price + labour band below.)

What genuinely moves the PHEV-1.5T replacement price is whether the engine and electric motor are supplied as a complete unit - they are often inseparable. The condition of the high‑voltage battery and inverter also affects viability - if the battery is degraded, investing in a powertrain replacement may not be worthwhile. The engine alone (without hybrid ancillaries) is rarely a viable purchase. See our full reconditioned engine cost guide.

failures.title: MG PHEV-1.5T Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: Hybrid system integration issues - 50k-100k miles
items.onset: 50,000-100,000 miles [PATTERN DATA - common on complex PHEV systems]
items.whatHappens: The PHEV-1.5T combines a 1.5‑litre turbo engine with an integrated electric motor, a clutch system between them, and sophisticated software to manage seamless transitions. Software glitches, sensor failures, or clutch wear can cause jerky transitions between electric and petrol power, reduced performance, or warning lights. This is a complex system where multiple components can cause similar symptoms.
items.repairVsReplace: Diagnosis is key - many issues are software‑addressable (dealer reflash) or sensor‑related. Hardware repair (clutch, electric motor) typically costs £800-£2,000. Complete powertrain replacement is rarely necessary unless the electric motor itself has failed.

items.title: Battery cooling system issues - 60k-100k miles
items.onset: 60,000-100,000 miles [PATTERN DATA - hybrid battery cooling is critical]
items.whatHappens: The high‑voltage battery in the PHEV-1.5T requires active liquid cooling. The cooling pump, hoses, or radiator can develop leaks or fail, leading to battery overheating, reduced performance, and in severe cases, battery degradation. This is more common on cars that do frequent short trips where the system never fully reaches operating temperature.
items.repairVsReplace: Cooling system repair costs £300-£800. If ignored, battery overheating can permanently degrade the battery pack, which is a £4,000-£8,000 replacement cost.

items.title: Timing chain stretch - 80k-120k miles (higher‑mileage units)
items.onset: 80,000-120,000 miles [PATTERN DATA - common on chain‑driven turbo petrol engines]
items.whatHappens: The 15E4E petrol engine component of the PHEV uses a chain‑driven timing system. On higher‑mileage units, the timing chain can stretch, leading to timing inaccuracy and rough running. This is less common on PHEV applications because the engine runs less frequently than in a conventional car, but it remains a known risk.
items.repairVsReplace: Chain and tensioner replacement costs £500-£1,000 if caught early (rattle on cold start). If the chain breaks, the engine is scrap.

failures.goodYearsLine: The PHEV-1.5T powertrain is considered generally reliable, with the hybrid system's complexity being the primary concern. Regular use (avoiding prolonged periods of battery‑only running) helps keep the engine and hybrid components healthy. Later production units (2022 onwards) have reportedly addressed some early software and cooling issues.

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the PHEV-1.5T
variants.intro: The PHEV-1.5T is a specific hybrid powertrain configuration, combining the 1.5‑litre turbo petrol engine (15E4E) with an integrated electric motor. It is distinct from the non‑hybrid 1.5‑litre turbo (15E4E) and the Atkinson‑cycle hybrid engine (15S4U). Where to find the code: The engine code is stamped on the engine block (15E4E) and the V5C registration document under "Engine number". However, the PHEV specification is confirmed by the presence of high‑voltage cabling, the electric motor housing, and the battery pack under the boot floor. Which codes get confused with it: The PHEV-1.5T is most often confused with: - 15E4E (petrol‑only) - same engine code but without the electric motor, inverter, and high‑voltage battery. Not a straight swap. - 15S4U (Atkinson‑cycle hybrid) - a completely different engine design (naturally aspirated, non‑turbo), used in the MG HS PHEV in some markets but not the UK. Not interchangeable. Why fitting the wrong revision matters: The PHEV-1.5T is a fully integrated system - the engine, electric motor, clutch, and ECU are all calibrated together. Fitting a non‑hybrid 15E4E will not work - the hybrid ECU will not recognise it, and the electric motor integration will be lost. Always confirm the exact PHEV specification before purchasing a replacement.

relatives.description: 15E4E (petrol‑only) - The 1.5‑litre turbo petrol engine that forms the combustion half of the PHEV powertrain. While the long block is the same, the PHEV version has different ancillaries, wiring, and ECU calibration. Not a straight swap - the hybrid system integration is missing.

15S4U (Atkinson‑cycle hybrid) - The naturally aspirated Atkinson‑cycle petrol engine used in some MG hybrid models. This is a different engine design (non‑turbo, different cam profiles) and is not interchangeable with the PHEV-1.5T.
E - Tech (full EV) - The pure‑electric motor used in MG4 and MG ZS EV. While both are electrified powertrains, the E-Tech has no combustion engine and is not related to the PHEV-1.5T.
The same PHEV architecture is used in Roewe and Maxus models in China. Specifications and mounting points may differ - not guaranteed to be a straight swap into an MG.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement PHEV-1.5T - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: A used PHEV-1.5T is only advisable if the complete powertrain (engine + electric motor + inverter) is supplied as a matched unit from a donor vehicle with known battery health. A bare engine without hybrid ancillaries is rarely viable. The key risks are: clutch wear between engine and motor, electric motor health, and software integration. Only buy from a specialist who can verify the hybrid system's health.

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: The recommended route for most PHEV-1.5T replacements. A proper recon includes: full engine rebuild with new timing chain and tensioner, electric motor bearing and seal replacement, clutch system overhaul, and a full inverter health check. For a £2,500-£4,500 investment, you get a 12-24 month warranty and a powertrain that should be good for another 80k+ miles. Ensure the reconditioner has specific PHEV experience.

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full PHEV-1.5T rebuild is generally only justified for numbers‑matching cars or where the block and motor housing are in pristine condition. Typical costs £4,000-£6,500. For most owners, reconditioned is the smarter and more cost‑effective choice.

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: All our vetted specialists offer supply‑only, supply‑and‑fit, or full workshop installation. Fitting a PHEV powertrain requires specialist hybrid training and high‑voltage safety certification - ensure your chosen garage is qualified. Fitting through the network includes a 12‑month warranty on parts and labour, with nationwide delivery to your chosen garage or home address.
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: The PHEV-1.5T is found in MG HS PHEV models, which typically hold values of £12,000-£25,000. At these price points, a £2,500+ recon is financially viable and usually sensible. However, consider the hybrid battery health as a deciding factor - if the battery is nearing end‑of‑life (typically 8-10 years), the combined replacement cost of engine + battery may exceed the car's value. Always compare the total cost of powertrain + battery repairs against the vehicle's market value.

items.question: How much does an MG PHEV-1.5T powertrain replacement cost?
items.answer: A reconditioned PHEV-1.5T typically costs £2,500-£4,500 supply-only, with fitted prices ranging from £3,190-£5,650 depending on labour and warranty. Used units are cheaper at £1,500-£3,500 supply-only but carry higher risk of hybrid system health. A full rebuild can exceed £6,500 if the electric motor and clutch require replacement. Fitting time is longer than conventional engines - 10-15 hours due to hybrid complexity.

items.question: What is the most common failure on the PHEV-1.5T?
items.answer: The most common issues are hybrid system integration problems - software glitches, sensor failures, or clutch wear that cause jerky transitions between electric and petrol power. Many issues are software-addressable (dealer reflash) rather than hardware failures. Battery cooling system leaks and timing chain stretch are also reported but less common. Diagnostic expertise is critical - not all garages understand PHEV systems.

items.question: Which MG models use the PHEV-1.5T?
items.answer: The PHEV-1.5T is fitted exclusively to the MG HS EHS (PHEV) - the plug-in hybrid variant of MG's flagship SUV. It is not used in the MG4, MG ZS, or MG3 - those are either pure EV or conventional petrol. The MG HS is also available with the 15E4E (petrol-only) - check your badge carefully.

items.question: Should I buy a used or reconditioned PHEV-1.5T?
items.answer: For most owners, a reconditioned PHEV-1.5T is the better choice because it includes a full rebuild of both engine and electric motor components, with a warranty covering the integrated system. Used units are only advisable if the complete powertrain (engine + electric motor + inverter) is supplied as a matched unit from a donor vehicle with known battery health. A bare engine without hybrid ancillaries is rarely viable. Only buy from specialists with PHEV experience and high-voltage certification.

items.answer: The engine code on the V5C may show 15E4E, but the presence of high‑voltage cabling, the electric motor housing, and the battery pack under the boot floor confirms PHEV specification. Enter your reg to confirm your specification

The badge on the tailgate will say "EHS" or "PHEV" - petrol‑only versions do not have this.
If your car has a charging port, it's definitely the PHEV‑1.5T.

items.question: Is the PHEV-1.5T reliable overall?
items.answer: Yes, the PHEV-1.5T is considered generally reliable when properly maintained. The hybrid system's complexity is the primary concern, but the engine itself is robust. Regular use (avoiding prolonged battery-only running) keeps the engine and hybrid components healthy. Regular oil changes every 10,000 miles or annually are essential for the petrol engine. The hybrid battery is generally more of a long-term concern than the powertrain itself.
